== Anagrams ==

* [[Warrant Officer M'Kae]] — Mark McKay, Mark Tuttle's radio name

== Career ==

In a 2018 interview Tuttle described SWCCG as "Tom and Rollie's game". He was recruited from ''Star Trek'' CCG community work into ''Star Wars'' playtesting around ''A New Hope''.<ref name="fantha" /> He took part in Decipher's in-house playtests from ''Star Wars'' CCG [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]] on, when they were held at the Omni hotel on the Waterside in Norfolk.<ref name="wr3" />

At [[DecipherCon 1999]] (11–14 November 1999) he and [[Ryan Morris]] ran Radio Free DecipherCon, Decipher's audio feed from the convention, which Decipher called "the voice and tech behind Radio Free DecipherCon".<ref name="dc99-audio" /> The Thursday feeds list him interviewing designers [[Evan Lorentz]] and [[Chuck Kallenbach]] and Star Wars CCG finalists.<ref name="dc99-thu">[http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/THU/index.html DecipherCon 1999 audio feeds: Thursday], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010217093703/http://www1.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/THU/index.html Internet Archive].</ref> Decipher's [[1999 Decipher World Championship|Star Wars CCG World Championship]] page carried his play-by-play of games 1 and 2 and his interview with finalists [[Gary Carman]] and [[Steven Lewis]].<ref name="dc99-sw" /> He and Morris closed the feed on Sunday.<ref name="dc99-sun">[http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/SUN/index.html DecipherCon 1999 audio feeds: Sunday], Decipher (1999): "Closing comments....and that's all folks (M. Tuttle, R. Morris)". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010217090821/http://www1.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/SUN/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

He was master of ceremonies at [[DecipherCon 2000]]. On [[Radio Free Decipher]] Broadcasts 50 and 51 he previewed the convention's new products, Day One start times and Decipher Olympics, and on Broadcast 53 he thanked the attendees and looked back on the weekend.<ref name="rfd50">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UhZv7OpkOwA Broadcast 50 - Radio Free Decipher (15 September, 2000): GenCon 2000 Celebrity Interviews], Player's Council (YouTube), 0:06–4:58. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-UhZv7OpkOwA Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="rfd51">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2tQmFqhsx74 Broadcast 51 - Radio Free Decipher (22 September, 2000): DecipherCon, Tom Lischke on Jabba's Sealed], Player's Council (YouTube), 0:05–5:29. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-2tQmFqhsx74 Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="rfd53">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hff_CPT5OY0 Broadcast 53 - Radio Free Decipher (13 October, 2000): Mark Tuttle, DecipherCon 2000 Recap], Player's Council (YouTube), 0:06–3:13. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-Hff_CPT5OY0 Internet Archive]</ref>

His radio shows followed the end of Radio Free Decipher.<ref name="rfd" /> On [[WARS Radio]] episodes 3 (9 July 2004) and 4 he interviewed [[Warren Holland]] on the origins of [[WARS TCG]].<ref name="wr3" />
